events.title: Internet Explorer 4.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft released Internet Explorer 4.0 in September 1997 with deeper Windows integration, Dynamic HTML, and the Trident rendering engine.
events.about: IE 4 turned the browser into part of the Windows shell — the desktop could show web folders and Active Desktop widgets. Trident became the engine behind IE for fifteen years and influenced how millions of intranet apps were built.

narrative.whyChosen: IE 4 marked Microsoft's boldest push to make the web indistinguishable from Windows.
narrative.whyImportant: Trident and DHTML gave developers rich client pages — but also years of IE-only site designs.
narrative.problemSolved: Microsoft needed a browser tightly woven into Windows to counter Netscape's cross-platform dominance.

events.title: JUnit released
events.summary: Kent Beck and Erich Gamma released JUnit in September 1997 — a unit testing framework that popularized automated test methods in Java.
events.about: JUnit's `@Test` annotations and assertion methods spawned xUnit ports in every language — pytest, RSpec, NUnit, Go testing. Test-driven development and CI pipelines assume the patterns JUnit established.

narrative.whyChosen: JUnit defined the xUnit family of testing frameworks.
narrative.whyImportant: It made automated unit tests a standard part of professional development.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers ran ad-hoc test mains; there was no lightweight test runner convention.
